findings.claim: The engine ships no Mannequin-to-MetaHuman retargeter. MetaHumanCharacter ships IK_MH_IKRig, which has chains for spine, neck, head, arms, legs and every finger, foot and hand IK goals, and the preview mesh /MetaHumanCharacter/Body/IdentityTemplate/SKM_Body. It also ships RTG_MH_IKRig, whose only IK rig is IK_MH_IKRig, so it retargets MetaHuman to MetaHuman. Epic recommends RTG_MH_IKRig ('optimized for MetaHuman full body IK solve') for putting template animations onto an assembled character. The project solved Mannequin to MetaHuman itself: IK_Quinn, IK_Physis and RTG_Quinn_To_Physis (auto chains and auto full-body IK) batch-retargeted all Mannequin sequences. That includes /Game/Characters/Physis/Animations/Physis_MM_Idle (plus a copy in AnimBP/), which uses /Game/MetaHumans/Common/.../metahuman_base_skel.

findings.claim: One idle can drive every MetaHuman assembled into the same Common folder, and each keeps its own proportions. In metahuman_base_skel, root uses 'Animation'. The whole FK chain uses 'AnimationRelative' (142 bones: pelvis, spine_01-05, neck_01-02, head, clavicles, arms, hands, main finger bones, legs and twist bones). The 193 helper bones use 'Animation', 4 bones use AnimationScaled and 3 use Skeleton. AnimationRelative applies the clip as a delta from its retarget-source pose onto each mesh's own reference rotation and translation. Remaining risk: arms clipping on much heavier or taller bodies. Epic retargets between MetaHuman body types to 'correct for any issues created by the difference in height or body type'.

findings.claim: How face and body are driven, in both BP_MetaHuman_Legacy and BP_MH_Physis. Components: Root, Body, Face, Torso, Legs, Feet, Hair, Eyebrows, Eyelashes, Fuzz, Mustache, Beard, LODSync and MetaHuman (MetaHumanComponentUE). The construction script has EnableMasterPose (GetChildrenComponents, then SetLeaderPoseComponent) and LiveLinkSetup (Use Live Link and Use ARKit; switches to ABP_MH_LiveLink, which holds the LiveLink pose and PA_MetaHuman_ARKit_Mapping). Body is the driver: the template sets no anim class, Physis uses Physis_ABP_Unarmed. The body mesh's post-process ABP_Body_PostProcess runs RigLogic body correctives plus CR_MetaHuman_HeadMovement_IK_Proc, which is 'needed only for animations created with MHA'. Face has anim class ABP_Face, which is a single CopyPoseFromMesh feeding the output pose. The face mesh's post-process ABP_Face_PostProcess runs CopyPoseFromMesh, RigLogic, the head IK rig and a layered blend. Clothing follows Body by leader pose, or by ABP_Clothing_PostProcess (CopyPoseFromMesh plus CR_PlaceHolder control rig plus RigidBody) when a physics asset or control rig is set. Epic's wording: 'MetaHumans are driven by the Body skeletal mesh component.' and 'The Face copies the bone transforms from the Body in its post-processing AnimBP using a Copy Pose From Mesh node.' Copy-pose costs more than leader-follower.

findings.claim: Cheapest face for an NPC with no facial animation: call SetLeaderPoseComponent(Body) on Face. A follower with a leader does not tick its own pose or AnimBPs, so no RigLogic runs. Follower bones the leader lacks, which are all FACIAL_* joints, keep their reference local pose under their parent, so the face stays neutral and moves with the head. The face skeleton's non-facial bones (root, pelvis, spine_01-05, clavicle and upperarm correctives, neck_01-02, head) match the body's names. The cost: no neck correctives and no blinking. The default ABP_Face plus post-process path keeps both, at RigLogic cost.

findings.claim: Minimum for a MetaHuman NPC that idles and turns. (1) Body: the MetaHuman body mesh playing an idle on /Game/MetaHumans/Common/.../metahuman_base_skel; its post-process runs automatically. (2) Face: a child of Body at identity transform with no socket, using ABP_Face or leader pose. (3) Groom components (hair, brows, lashes, beard if any) on the Face, each with its binding. Bindings target that exact face mesh: Hair_M_Layered_Binding has TargetSkeletalMesh SKM_MH_Physis_FaceMesh. (4) Optional: LODSync and a MetaHuman component. Not needed: LiveLink, Control Rig, the Torso/Legs/Feet components and the template's construction-script graphs. Turning needs nothing new, because BP_NPC already rotates the whole actor toward Physis.

findings.claim: How BP_NPC drives the Mannequin people today. BP_NPC is an Actor with DefaultSceneRoot, Body (SkeletalMeshComponent), Shape (StaticMeshComponent) and Lower/Upper/Head (StaticMeshComponents). Both the construction script and BeginPlay call AttachComponentToComponent with KeepRelative: Lower to pelvis, Upper to spine_05, Head to head. BeginPlay calls PlayAnimation(MM_Idle, looping), then SetPosition at a random 0-1.5 s. EventTick uses RInterpTo to turn the actor toward Physis while talking, only if the bool variable 'Face' is true. TalkStart, TalkEnd and the Hold countdown in EventTick switch TickableWhenPaused on the actor and on Body only. wear() sets SKM_<Manny|Quinn>_Simple and puts MI_CP_<skin> on material slots 0-1. It sets each garment's world transform to the actor's at the bind pose and attaches it KEEP_WORLD to its bone, then sets ANIMATION_SINGLE_NODE and override_animation_data(MM_Idle). fitting() checks does_socket_exist(bone) and a 50 cm reach.

findings.claim: What changes in that code for MetaHumans. MM_IDLE (conclave_logic.py:74) and IDLE (scenario:58) must name a metahuman_base_skel idle such as /Game/Characters/Physis/Animations/Physis_MM_Idle, and the BeginPlay graph must be rewritten after the change (the module's own rule, lines 20-21). wear() must stop putting MI_CP skins on Body slots 0-1 (scenario:714-716) and must also set the face mesh, grooms and bindings per person. The Face and its grooms need the same TickableWhenPaused switching as Body. Otherwise talks, which pause the game, may show a breathing body under a frozen head. The existing bool member 'Face' (conclave_logic.py:243, 447, 453; scenario:783) clashes with a component named 'Face'. Either give the component another name and set the MetaHuman component's FaceComponentName to match, or rename the bool.

findings.claim: Attaching garments still works mechanically, but the current garments will not fit. pelvis, spine_05, head and hand_l/hand_r exist on the MetaHuman body. The body mesh defines no sockets, only bones, so AttachComponentToComponent and fitting() work unchanged. The garments, however, are modelled in actor space over the Mannequin bind pose (people.py puts the head bone at 1.625 m). Reference-pose bone heights for head / spine_05 / pelvis: Quinn_Simple 162.5 / 139.5 / 98.7 cm, Manny_Simple 162.6 / 141.1 / 95.9 cm, Physis's MetaHuman 152.1 / 127.2 / 94.0 cm. Placed the current way, garments would sit about 10-12 cm too high on a body like hers, and every MetaHuman has its own reference pose. Garments belong on Body, not Face; Head items follow the face because the face copies Body's head. Grooms will not collide with hats (inferred).

recommendation:
Keep BP_NPC and its talk and turn logic, add the MetaHuman parts to it, and play the idle the project already retargeted.
1. Assemble the 12 looks with Physis's settings: UE Optimized, Medium, into /Game/MetaHumans, with Common in /Game/MetaHumans/Common. All of them then share /Game/MetaHumans/Common/Female/Medium/NormalWeight/Body/metahuman_base_skel.
2. In BP_NPC, keep 'Body' as the driver. Add a face SkeletalMeshComponent as a child of Body at identity, with no socket. Name it something other than 'Face', or rename the bool. Add groom components under the face, and a LODSync. A MetaHuman component is optional; if you add it, set its FaceComponentName.
3. In wear(), per person: set Body to SKM_<Name>_BodyMesh with no MI_CP skin override, the face to SKM_<Name>_FaceMesh, and the grooms with their bindings. For the cheapest neutral face, call SetLeaderPoseComponent(Body) on the face. For neck correctives and optional blinking, give it ABP_Face and let its post-process run, at RigLogic cost.
4. Point MM_IDLE (conclave_logic.py:74) and IDLE (scenario:58) at /Game/Characters/Physis/Animations/Physis_MM_Idle and rewrite the BeginPlay graph. Test it first on the tallest and heaviest bodies. If the arms clip, batch-retarget per body with RTG_MH_IKRig or with the project's make_retargeter pattern. Do not rely on playing MM_Idle through bone-name remapping.
5. Add the face and grooms wherever Body's TickableWhenPaused is switched.
6. Keep attaching to Body bones (pelvis, spine_05, head), but regenerate each garment against that MetaHuman's bind pose. Better for realistic skin: move the clothes to skinned meshes on metahuman_base_skel that follow Body by leader pose, the SK_Physis_Outfit route.
Do not copy the BP_MH template graphs into NPCs; they bring the LiveLink graph and its ABP_MH_LiveLink reference. Skip MetaHuman Crowd.

findings.claim: What skin U and V mean. They are UI coordinates in [0,1]^2 on the texture-synthesis model's 2-D skin-tone map. U maps linearly onto the model axis v0, whose range is set by v0_range in ts_params.json. V maps onto a v1 range that depends on v0. There is no axis flip (v_ui_axis_transform 0). Epic's own toolset documents U as lightness (0 light, 1 dark) and V as redness (0 cool, 1 red), with these examples: very pale cool [0.06,0.12], pale [0.10,0.45], light warm [0.18,0.75], medium neutral [0.50,0.45], olive [0.50,0.30], tan golden [0.60,0.65], medium-dark cool [0.72,0.12], dark neutral [0.85,0.45], very dark warm [0.93,0.75], darkest reddish brown [0.98,0.88]. U < 0.5 picks the light body albedo T_Skin_V1, otherwise V2, and the body is tinted by a bias/gain the synthesizer computes.

findings.claim: Sign-in. Authentication goes through EOS. CINEMATIC: all face LODs 0-7 and all body LODs 0-3. bBakeMaterials=true and bUsePreBakedGrooms=true. Source caps: animated albedo deltas 512, animated normal deltas 1024. Baked head maps: LOD0 normal and SRMF 8192, base colour 2048, scatter 512; LOD1-2 at 4096; LOD3-4 at 2048; LOD5-7 at 1024. Eyes 2048, body base colour 4096. LODSync has 8 LODs and grooms are left at full strands. HIGH: face LODs [1,3,5,7], all body LODs, its own Face_LODSettings_High and Body_LODSettings_High. Caps add base colour 1024, normal 2048 and cavity 2048. Template _High: LODSync 4 LODs, RigLogic LOD threshold 2. Strands are decimated to their LOD1 setting, card LOD1 and LOD3 are kept, and the LOD6 mesh is dropped. MEDIUM: face LODs [3,5,7], body LODs [1,2,3]. build_meta_human needs a real GPU editor session, because -nullrhi turns off the Texture Graph engine that does the material baking. With about 3.5 of the 8 GB of VRAM held by other apps, Cinematic and High bakes at 8K and 4K risk the Vulkan out-of-memory crashes this project has had. The author should close other apps and launch the editor with -noraytracing for builds. The project's history of out-of-memory kills, plus one forum claim that assembly needs more than 32 GB of RAM (unverified; this machine has 31 GB), means one character should be built and measured first.

Several features cannot be reached from Python: applying a preset, region blending, the fixed legacy body types, head scale and gizmo moves. The workarounds are to duplicate a preset with duplicate_asset, blend face coefficients, use the body constraints, and sculpt with translate_face_landmarks.

Clothing: the only shipped garment is a T-shirt and shorts (WI_DefaultGarment), recolourable through four colour parameters. Palette garments that look like the Conclave's own would need new MetaHumanWardrobeItem assets wrapping a ChaosOutfitAsset or a skinned SkeletalMesh; I have not verified that Python can set them up. The existing static SM_CP_G_* meshes cannot be added as MetaHuman wardrobe items.

Integration with the game: the build produces a standalone Actor Blueprint (BP_<Name>, derived from BP_MetaHuman_Legacy) on the MetaHuman skeleton, not a BP_NPC. Wiring it into BP_NPC (talk interaction, idle animation, garment attachment) is separate work. I did not verify whether MM_Idle plays on the MetaHuman body without retargeting.

There is no offline fallback that keeps both the original face and an assembled MetaHuman. Without the cloud, the most you get is export_geometry (sculpted head and body meshes on the archetype's uncalibrated rig, with grey materials) plus the transient 1k synthesized textures. Turning that into finished characters would need a custom, untested material path.
recommendation:
Build one character first: Listener, in a GPU editor launched with -noraytracing and other apps closed. Then loop the same script over the other 18. The order matters: face, then body, then skin (including face_texture_index), all before auto-rig; auto-rig before the texture download; textures before the build.

Sequence, all through S = unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.MetaHumanCharacterEditorSubsystem):

1. Create the asset. Either duplicate the nearest preset, `ch = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.duplicate_asset('/MetaHumanCharacter/Optional/Presets/<Name>', '/Game/Characters/Conclave/MHC_<Who>')`, or create one with `unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(name, path, unreal.MetaHumanCharacter, unreal.MetaHumanCharacterFactoryNew())`. Then set `ch.preview_material_type = unreal.MetaHumanCharacterSkinPreviewMaterial.EDITABLE` and call `S.try_add_object_to_edit(ch)`. Use try/finally so `S.remove_object_to_edit(ch)` always runs.
2. Face. Blend preset coefficient vectors with `S.get_face_model_coefficients` / `S.set_face_model_coefficients`; the presets must be duplicated into /Game and opened for editing, and quaternions re-normalized after mixing. Add small `S.translate_face_landmarks(ch, idx, deltas)` moves, then `S.commit_face_state(ch)`. For Listener (the First One), push the coefficients a little past the preset space instead of making extreme landmark moves: the landmark path enforces no bounds.
3. Body. `cons = S.get_body_constraints(ch, False)`. Set `is_active` and `target_measurement` for Height (in cm), Masculine/Feminine, Fat, Muscularity and any measurements needed. Then `S.set_body_constraints(ch, cons)`, `S.commit_body_state(ch)`, `unreal.MetaHumanGeneratorSubsystemWrapper.reset_neck_to_body(ch)` and `S.commit_face_state(ch)`.
4. Skin, with natural tones. `ss = ch.skin_settings`. Set `ss.skin.u` (lightness, 0 light to 1 dark) and `ss.skin.v` (redness, 0 cool to 1 red). Pick `ss.skin.face_texture_index` from 0-152 using texture_attributes.json (wrinkles, stubble, marks), and `ss.skin.body_texture_index` from 0-8. Set freckles and accents, keep `desired_texture_sources_resolutions` at 2k, then `S.commit_skin_settings(ch, ss)`.
5. Eyes, makeup, lashes and teeth. `S.commit_eyes_settings` (iris primary/secondary U = warmth, V = brightness), `S.commit_makeup_settings`, and `hm = ch.head_model_settings; hm.eyelashes.type = ...; S.commit_head_model_settings(ch, hm)`.
6. Grooms and clothing. `pc = S.get_preview_collection(ch)`, then `key = pc.try_add_item_from_wardrobe_item('Hair'|'Eyebrows'|'Beard'|'Mustache'|'Peachfuzz'|'Outfits', unreal.load_asset(path))` and `pc.default_instance.try_add_slot_selection(unreal.MetaHumanPipelineSlotSelection(slot_name=..., selected_item=key))`. Then `S.on_edit_preview_collection(ch)` and `S.assemble_for_preview(ch)`. Set palette colours through instance parameters (hair DyeColor; garment PrimaryColorShirt, SecondaryColorShirt, PrimaryColorShort, SecondaryColorShort), then call `S.on_edit_preview_collection(ch)` again.
7. Cloud. `S.request_auto_rigging(ch, params)` with `rig_type=JOINTS_ONLY`, `blocking=True`, `report_progress=False`, then `S.request_texture_sources(ch, params)` with `blocking=True`, `report_progress=False`. Turn on the CVar `MetaHuman.Cloud.Autorig.UseDdc 1` so reruns of an unchanged face cost nothing. Reusing a few face_texture_index values across the cast lets texture downloads come from the local cache.
8. Build. `if S.can_build_meta_human(ch, True)`, build with `MetaHumanCharacterEditorBuildParameters`: `pipeline_type=OPTIMIZED`, `pipeline_quality=MEDIUM` (LOW for background people; HIGH only for close-ups, since it keeps decimated strand hair and 4 face LODs), `absolute_build_path='/Game/MetaHumans'`, `common_folder_path='/Game/MetaHumans/Common'`. Avoid CINEMATIC on this 8 GB GPU. Save the character and the output folders, and place BP_<Name> or adapt BP_NPC.

If the cloud keeps timing out from Greece, stop and ask the author to choose between a US VPN or WARP, or dropping the MetaHuman route.

recommendation:
Yes, this machine can render them, but only as 12 lean MetaHumans, and not in a ray-traced editor that is already full (measured: the Conclave alone filled 4.58-4.76 GB with RT on).

1) Pipeline: in the MetaHuman Creator Assembly tool, use UE Optimized (the legacy actor Blueprint) at High for all 12 people. Reuse each person's assembled Blueprint for their repeat rows (Thanks, Done, Spire), so the 19 placed BP_NPCs load only 12 sets of assets.
   - Not UE Cine: Epic gives it 1-2 GB per character, 8K LOD0 maps and a 669-blendshape LOD0.
   - Not Medium: the best face LOD is source LOD3, which is 3,789 vertices in the existing MH_Physis, too coarse for face-to-face dialogue, and 5.8 has a known issue with long messy hair cards at Medium.
   - Not Low: hair is helmets only.
   - Not MetaHumanCrowd: it is experimental and built on Mass and instanced meshes, uses face LOD2-3 and card hair, and is not meant for placed dialogue actors. Keep it in mind for a distant crowd in the Commons later.

2) Textures: keep the default 2K source download.
   - Before each build, open Assembly > Textures, press Refresh, and set every output to 2048 or less:
     - top face LOD (LOD1): normal, SRMF and basecolor 2048, scatter 512;
     - face LOD3: 1024; face LOD5-7: 512;
     - body basecolor, normal and SRMF: 2048 (1024 where clothes cover the body);
     - eyes: 1024 (512 for minor people); teeth: 512.
   - After the build, check that no texture is 4K or 8K; MH_Physis came out with an 8192x8192 body basecolor.
   - For minor people, consider Scalable Normals (basecolor 512, SRMF 1K, normal 1K, plus shared pore normals).
   - Leave virtual textures on (the 5.8 default), so the face and body maps stay within the virtual-texture pools.

3) Hair: cards for everyone.
   - Tick Use Cards on every GroomComponent, or set r.HairStrands.MinLOD 3, or set r.HairStrands.UseCardsInsteadOfStrands 1.
   - Set binding to Rigid on the card and helmet LODs and turn hair simulation off.
   - Check that eyelashes and peach fuzz still show, because forcing cards hides any groom part that has no cards.
   - Allow strands, at most, on the Listener during RT screenshot sessions.

4) Ray tracing: turn off Visible in Ray Tracing on all GroomComponents, or set r.HairStrands.Raytracing 0, and never enable Use Hair Raytracing Geometry. Use r.RayTracing.Geometry.SkeletalMeshes.LODBias 1 in play and 2 in the editor. For layout-only sessions, use r.RayTracing.Geometry.SkeletalMeshes 2.

5) LOD: keep High's LOD sync (4 LODs, face screen sizes 0.5/0.2/0.1/0.05) and r.SkeletalMeshLODBias 0 for close dialogue. Set the LOD sync Min LOD to 1 on people who are only ever seen from far away.

6) Nanite stays off; MetaHumans do not need it.

7) Editor procedure:
   - Assemble and place in a -noraytracing editor with other apps closed.
   - Put r.Streaming.PoolSize 400 after any sg.TextureQuality in -ExecCmds, because sg.TextureQuality 3 resets the pool to 1000.
   - Turn RT on only for shots.
   - Run a pilot first: assemble 2 people, place all 19 BP_NPCs, and measure with stat RHI, rhi.DumpResourceMemory, r.SkinCache.PrintMemorySummary and stat GPU.
   - Aim for 0.5 GB or less for all MetaHumans together, and assemble the other 10 only if the pilot fits.

The total VRAM and the frame time on this GPU are unknown until that pilot is measured.
